title: In front of the house
goal: Say in front of, behind, outside and around, and move things onto, into, out of and towards with the dative and the ablative.

intro.text: *öň* (front), *yz* (back), *daş* (outside) and *töwerek* (surroundings) work like *üst*: *öýüň öňünde*, in front of the house. Change the case for movement: the dative for where to (*stoluň üstüne*, onto the table; *Merdanyň ýanyna*, to see Merdan), the ablative for where from (*sumkanyň içinden*, out of the bag).

exercises.question: How do you say **in front of the house**?

why.1: After the rounded *ö* of *öň*, the vowel rounds: *öňünde*.

exercises.en: The car is behind the house.

reject.why: After the genitive *öýüň*, *yz* takes **its** and the *n*: *yzynda*.

exercises.label: *öň* with **my, your…** and the locative: in front of me, in front of you…
exercises.explain: The second syllable rounds after *ö*: *öňümde*, *öňüňde*, *öňünde*; the third keeps *i*: *öňümizde*.

exercises.prompt: Put the book on the table! (to a friend)
exercises.explain: Where to put it: the dative, *üstüne*, onto. *Kitaby*, the book, as a definite object.

accept: I am going to see Aýna.

exercises.question: *Ol sumkanyň içinden telefon çykardy.* What did she do?
options: She took a phone out of the bag.
She put a phone into the bag.
She looked for a phone in the bag.
She left the phone next to the bag.

why.1: **Into the bag** would be *içine*, with the dative.

exercises.explain: *içinden*, from the inside, with *çykarmak*, to take out: she took a phone out of the bag.

exercises.prompt: The bus stop is in front of the post office.

reject.why: After the *ö* of *öň*, the vowel rounds: *öňünde*.

exercises.explain: *poçtanyň öňünde*, in front of the post office.

exercises.en: The children are playing outside the house.

exercises.text: There are many shops around the square.
accept: Around the square there are many shops.
The cat came out from under the bed.
The cat [got|crawled] out from under the bed.

exercises.question: Which form means **to Merdan's, to see Merdan**?

why.1: *ýanynda* is **at Merdan's, next to him**: no movement.
why.3: Merdan takes the genitive, not the dative: *Merdanyň*.

exercises.prompt: Come over to me! (to a friend)
exercises.explain: *ýan* + *-ym* (my) + *-a*: *ýanyma*, to my side, over to me.
